fences.rule: If the move is the first one, a party destroying its own outside option in the other's sight so that cooperation can start, it is First cut there; if it is the standing hold the counterparty then has, a flow of custom it can cut, it is Tap read from the seller's side here.
fences.case: The supplier who tooled a line for one customer and is bound by that customer's orders because leaving strands the investment.

fences.rule: There the hostage is handed over unrequested as a first move that starts cooperation; here the same token is the standing hold, which lasts exactly as long as the token cannot be duplicated and fails by reissue.
fences.case: The passport an employer holds under kafala, unmade the day a replacement passport is issued.

fences.rule: If the hold is named as a bare noun phrase with no carrier, no market born of it, no escape, and no time-to-acquire, it is there; if it is named with all five it is here.
fences.case: Slashable collateral as a bare mechanism that makes cooperation stable.

fences.rule: Cosigner presupposes Vouching there, reputation staked on another's behalf as a good, and names the conversion: the guarantor's hold on the principal sold to the creditor priced in cash the creditor can hold.
fences.case: The parent who cosigns a student's lease so that a landlord with no hold on the student rents anyway.

fences.rule: The same registry, list, or exemption read from the bound party's side is a floor there, and read from the counterparty's side is a hold here: Passport trade becomes Portable file, Hiring hall becomes Place in line, Tools the bailiff cannot take becomes the exempt class Seizable title is carved around.
fences.case: The nurse hired in a town where nobody knows her on the strength of the licensing board's record.

fences.rule: If the question is who may bring a harm before a tribunal, it is Deputized injury there; if the question is whether any hold reaches the party's purse so that a promise to it can be enforced, it is Someone to sue here, and the two come apart.
fences.case: The river given a legal guardian who can sue for its pollution, to which nobody will lend because no hold reaches the guardian's purse.
